Saw a couple of people ask wonder how i do my motion designs and in general how to become better. Here are some tips that can help:

1. Download a motion design video you really love and then analyse it in whatever tool you use. Check how long it takes, try to match the easings, how are the staggering between. Recreate it. This way you also get a feel why some one does something

2. Learn about the fundamentals of motion design. Check the 12 motion principles by disney. Look for advanced motion courses etc

3. Find inspiration in other forms of motion. animation (anime, short films), dance videos, sword swinging videos, parkour videos, listen to music and get a feel of the rhythm etc

Motion is all about story telling and every good story needs overall pace, differing tempo, intonations, space to breath etc

And also be very honest with yourself about your practising routine - if you do a motion design every week or just a half hearted version each day you won't improve. Challenge yourself. Do what's hard.

Most founders want a website shipped in 2 weeks.

But when they show me the website they want I have to tell them that the branding phase alone probably took a minimum of 4 weeks.

One of my biggest challenges as a project lead is explaining to the client that you have 3 choices:

- High quality with a longer timeline
- Shorter timeline with mediocre result
- Increased budget for both high quality and a short timeline

Of course the last one no one wants haha. So it’s kinda tricky - especially when clients come specifically to me because of my quality of work. 

And besides the timeline friction there’s the general issue with most founders not knowing the price for a well designed and developed website. 

When I work on projects I mostly work with a team of people whose skill reflect the quality the client and I want to achieve. 

And this just requires a higher budget and a reasonable time to deliver the best possible result. 

I rather not work with a client than to  disappoint and loose them by promising unrealistic expectations (happened to me before)

So yeah dear founders take your
time (or increase your budget) 🙂‍↕️🙏🏻

Be it branding, web design, motion design, product design etc - always look outside your box.

If you just look at websites for your web design project, or motion videos for your motion project you'll only have a limited source of inspiration.

Go watch a master swing a katana in beautiful flows, learn about brutalism, bauhaus, etc in architecture, visit  a indie art event where they create noise music, read a fantasy epic and be swallowed into the author's world (recommend way of kings lol).

I've learned that inspiration and creating good design isn't "i see something, i replicate it and adapt it" - ofc sometimes you can have very clear inspirations like that.

But many times it's an emotion you get by watching art or coming up w ideas that slumbered in the back of your mind because this experimental music unlocked a new perspective.

Enjoy the part of creation that is digesting your surroundings. 

You'll get a far better sense of good design & craft rather than just trying to copy good designs you see online

It’s a valid take seeing it as a designer who also wants to design not engineer.

I doubt tho that 20% of the top design (engineers) are better than 80% of coders - even if those developers don’t have an eye for design they are still much
more knowledgeable about coding than most design “engineers”

Esp good code requires extensive knowledge and learning of new standards that most vibe coders don’t care about. 

AI is a tool and using a tool requires being knowledgeable in that field. You can build something w AI, yes, but you didn’t code it. You wrote a prompt. I doubt many design “engineers” even know what object-oriented means.

I can use claude code to create me a prototype of something or to build something for myself but I would never ship something to a client or publish it w monetary interest.

There’s just too much I don’t know…and also don’t wanna know. I want to move rectangles around, not try figure out how to use ffmpeg to add main keyframes to a video cause it’s buggy on scroll. 

I see design engineering esp going from design to development bit like Heisenberg’s Uncertainty Principle. You either can measure the impulse or the position of a particle but never both. Similarly w becoming really great at something you have to choose where to focus. 

ofc you can get better at both but there will always be designers and developers who are better at it because they spent decades on perfecting it.

I love to fully engulf myself in design, art, creativity and visual creation. Even just walking through a new neighbourhood, seeing a cool building, have an interesting talk w a friend - all add to it. 

I don’t think I could do my best design work when I have to split my attention and effort trying to become a good developer as well

There are extremely talented creative developers who have an amazing sense of aesthetic and taste…and also designers shipping tools as addition to their branding/website. Which is amazing to see! 

But even those top design engineers and creative devs will prob see some limitations in their work by focusing on both designing and building.

Back then I was almost ready to leave design behind for good. The work culture sucked ass. I’ve got ptsd from looking at slack cause u only got messages when something didn’t work…no real praise.

This plus them time tracking u down to the last minute (you didn’t just had to work 8hrs but u had to track 8hrs on work) was killing my self-esteem and love for design.

Since I became freelance 2 years ago I’ve shipped more projects, made more money and worked way less.

For me I rather work 7 days a week with 4-6hrs focused work per day - some days i didn’t work at all. I just didn’t feel it and it was fine. I was out on a bike in thailand and suddenly the idea struck me.

It was like a force of nature pulling me towards creating what I feel speaks my truth.

And then the real journey begins - while yes you finished understanding a bit of the basic fundamentals and how to somehow get to a end result in your style, your curiosity and desire to explore who you are will lead you down a new path that i would call the journey of mastery. 

You will look at the fundamentals in a new and more experienced but also more directional way. You will feel even more depressed if you fail because it means you’ve failed “yourself” not someone else’s vision.

It’s a fascinating and rewarding journey. Becoming great at what you do is actually only a side effect. You’ll become a completely new human. 

Because what you create is so intertwined with who you are, there’s no other way then changing yourself when walking down this path.

I’m grateful to be able to experience this almost spiritual endeavour. And I know nobody will ever achieve full mastery. There will always be something to learn.

But that’s life. Like a river constantly flowing, constantly changing shape while still maintaining unity so will your journey be a continuous river of change while at the same time being one immovable constant.

“Did I charge too low?” - if you never hear you are too pricey, you’re definitely underpricing. Just raise it with the next project

“If he accepts, can I deliver the quality valued at that price?” - u set the price because you know ur value. If you never heard of a client that they’re not satisfied w your work, you’re good. Also remember there prob are shitty designers charging more than and still get jobs.

“Was I rude to ask for so much?” - no. you set your price. if the client is shocked or can’t afford you he just needs someone else. If they talk down to you why you’re so expensive, they’re just jealous they can’t get your services for a cheaper price

if you're starting out w web design or feel like you've hit a plateau i recommend doing some of these or all:

- go on awwwards, take one site and rebuild it - you'll learn soo much
- learn the principles of design - spacing, visual hierarchy etc. many junior designers lack esp in these areas. a great design is great because the designer completely understood the fundamentals
- experiment - just go wild for once. don't think about the trends or what you should do, just have fun.
- go to museums, read fiction books, actively listen to a song/album - submerging yourself into art gets your mind into a creative introspective mood. very important to strengthen your connection to creativity
- go outside and talk a way without your phone - taking everything can relax your mind and open you up to new ideas
- ask other designers (more senior than you) for feedback - many times we need the perspective of an experienced designer to break our boxed in view. can also be any creative person 
- find a way to create art that isn't design - be it painting, writing poetry, dancing. these forms of art are much purer in it's purpose than design is. It allows you to connect w your creativity on a much deeper level and gives you new perspectives
- buy some books about graphic design - not the "how to" but w real life examples. get inspired by other designers.

These are just some ideas you can utilise in your process to level up your skill. It's very important to do things over and over again to hone your craft but sometimes we're at a dead end and can't seem to get better at what we do. No matter how hard we try. 

Hope these help. If you have any tips to go from junior to senior, from good to great, please feel free to write them down in the comments. 🙌🏻

a well designed button in product design isn't flashy. 

it's functional, scaleable and adaptable. 

think about components like an ecosystem within an ecosystem.

a button on its own is very simple. but many different elements have different requirements for a button. 

some need an icon on the left, some need an icon on the right. some need the button to stretch and some need it to be smaller.

working from a molecular level up is the key to a powerful and scalable design system. 

(also the devs will thank you when you create modular based components)

A lot of the posts that go viral here are just flashy. 

Look closer and you see a lot of issues.

The whole GO / Loud Ring section feels unpleasant to click and unbalanced. And the AM/PM has a gap on the right. 

That's just some issues but the overall thing is that just because you see a post like this go viral doesn't mean it's well executed.

Why do you think concepts and flashy things like this get hyped but features that are implemented in real products aren't?

It's because they're made to work effortlessly not to wow you. I guarantee if you'd use this component long enough you'd see many issues that aren't even visible in this screenshot.

So if you really want to learn good product design learn from existing applications. Use mobbin, download apps, demo test saas tools. 

You'll learn from real and highly skillful product designers.
